# Free tutorial: Rewrite a bad ticket in five minutes

Turn a ticket nobody can act on into a triage note the next analyst can use.

The files for this seminar are in `~/case` (Linux) and `case/` (Python): `alerts.json`, `handover-night.txt`, `invoice.eml`, `mail.log`, `process.csv`, `proxy.log`, `share_listing.txt`, `ticket-88213.txt`.

## 1. The setting

This free tutorial is one step from **Seminar F: Evidence, notes and handoffs**. Turn a ticket nobody can act on into a triage note the next analyst can use.

The evidence is in `~/case`. Read the README there if you want the whole story.

## 2. A ticket nobody can act on

Most security work is handed from one person to the next: helpdesk to SOC, SOC to the incident lead, night shift to morning shift. If the note is poor, the next person starts again from zero, and an attack keeps running while they do.

Read helpdesk ticket 88213 and last night's handover. Both are real kinds of notes analysts receive every day.

- [ ] Which facts in the ticket have a time and a source?
- [ ] Which words are guesses ("probably", "maybe", "???")?
- [ ] What does the next person need that isn't there: which host, which user, which alert, what was done?
- [ ] What is wrong with "all quiet. couple of alerts, nothing major"?

> Hint: A useful note answers five questions: what fired, what I checked, what I found, what I don't know, and what happens next.

?> Which message ID did dev.kapoor report as phishing? :: sha256:3b4c868aaed95ad3038a9cf3f9d3aac10231f741a5500448dc1f2bba9fbbc5ae
?> At what time (HH:MM) did the helpdesk pull the cable on the HR PC? :: sha256:fdf6b948b07448b5dad617e71a41f1a1fb3a25b5f9ac5e2e2adf48410cd1f02a

cd ~/case
cat ticket-88213.txt
echo ---
cat handover-night.txt

## 3. Write the triage note

Now rewrite ticket 88213 as a triage note for alert **AL-2203**. The report builder checks each section as you type: it wants an alert ID, times with a time zone, the exact searches you ran, at least one gap, a disposition and an owner.

Rules that make notes useful:

- One time zone for everything (UTC here), written every time.
- Facts say where you saw them. Guesses go under "What I don't know yet".
- Write what you ran, so the next person can repeat it without asking you.

- [ ] Fill every section, then press Check the report
- [ ] Compare yours with the model answer only after you've written your own
- [ ] Download the Markdown: it is part of your hand-in

> Hint: "What I don't know yet" is never empty. Here: did the other two people open the invoice, and was anything copied out?

```tool report
{"tpl": "triage", "title": "Triage note: AL-2203 macro document on hr-pc07", "text": "# Triage note: AL-2203 macro document on hr-pc07

## What fired

AL-2203 "Office document with macros opened from the internet", severity high, host hr-pc07, user priya.nair, 2026-11-02 09:02:44 UTC.

## What I checked

- mail.log: grep 4A1F21C02 (the reported message)
- proxy.log: grep -E 'docm|s2.bin'
- process.csv: the process tree for hr-pc07 (Python cell, step 3)
- alerts.json: the other alerts on hr-pc07 between 09:00 and 10:00 UTC

## What I found

- 08:51 UTC: message 4A1F21C02 from bounce-7781@kestrel-logistlcs.com (look-alike domain, 203.0.113.45) was delivered to 3 people: priya.nair, dev.kapoor, tomas.reyes.
- 09:02 UTC: 10.20.0.14 downloaded INV-30412.docm from kestrel-logistlcs.com (proxy TCP_MISS/200).
- 09:02:55 UTC: WINWORD.EXE started cmd.exe, which started a hidden PowerShell running C:\Users\Public\upd.ps1.
- 09:03:09 UTC: hr-pc07 downloaded s2.bin from cdn-update-check.net (198.51.100.140).
- 09:03:20 UTC: PowerShell started C:\Users\Public\svchost-upd.exe (PID 4810).
- 09:41 UTC: PID 4810 mapped \\fs01\shared and started renaming files to .kestrel-locked (AL-2208).

## What I don't know yet

- Whether dev.kapoor or tomas.reyes opened the attachment (10.20.0.15 was blocked at 09:20 UTC; the third person is unknown).
- What s2.bin does, and whether data was copied out before the encryption.
- Whether other hosts talked to 198.51.100.140.

## Disposition and why

True positive, escalate: a macro document from a look-alike domain started PowerShell and an unknown program, and the same program is encrypting the file share.

## Next step and owner

Escalate to the incident lead now (09:55 UTC). Owner: SOC analyst on shift until the incident lead takes it; keep hr-pc07 off the network and do not reboot it.
", "n": 6, "blank": ["text"]}
```

?> Which disposition fits AL-2203? (escalate, handled, benign, false positive or more information) :: sha256:f965e5fbf98dd531b7c0fd4f9bdc8dd6df79f623c8345b8aa1b7cd756d317dd8

## 4. Where next

That was one step of **Seminar F: Evidence, notes and handoffs**. The full seminar has the video, every step in three levels (walkthrough, practice and solo), a graded hand-in and a certificate.
